identityTest.stableIdentity: A governed authorization domain and each effective permission grant remain identifiable across account changes, role assignment turnover, review conclusions and credential rotation.
identityTest.versionIdentity: Changes to role definition, action set, resource scope, conditions, basis, validity or delegation chain create immutable revisions or successor grants while preserving prior authorization evidence.

owns: principal, action, resource scope, condition, basis, justification and validity bindings

references.purpose: Digital account bound to an identity anchor

excludes: credential secret values or reversible digests

invariants: Person, identity anchor, digital account and principal reference remain linked but never equated.
An IAM access role is never inferred from an organizational role, title or position.
Every effective grant states principal, authority basis, justification, actions, resource scope, conditions and validity.
A delegated grant is a subset of source actions, scope and validity and preserves or strengthens source conditions.
A delegated grant cannot outlive or remain active after revocation of its source grant.
Consent may support disclosure but never creates general IAM capability, and an IAM grant never proves consent.
Access-review conclusions never revoke access until an effective grant transition is recorded.
Revocation propagation may be partial and partial propagation is a first-class non-success state.
Cached sessions and tokens cannot remain authorized beyond the supporting grant validity.
Secret values and reversible secret representations are prohibited from all registry records and projections.
Every approval, exercise, rotation, suspension and revocation correlates to append-only audit evidence.
Retired domain, role and grant identifiers remain resolvable and are never recycled.
holds: Registry namespace and identifier allocation are pending and no identifier may be guessed.
